name: Estonian Championships
content:
The Estonian Football Championship was established in 1921 and held 19 official seasons until 1940, when Estonia was occupied by the Soviet Union. During this period, the competition changed names several times: it was known as A-klass (1921–1923), I klass (1924–1926), and Liiduklass (1927–1940).

The early years were dominated by Sport Tallinn, which won a total of nine titles, making it the most successful club of the era. Other notable teams included Kalev Tallinn and Tallinna Jalgpalli Klubi, both of which secured multiple championships during the 1920s.

In the mid-to-late 1930s, Estonia Tallinn emerged as the leading club, winning five consecutive titles between 1934 and 1939. The final official championship before World War II was won by Olümpia Tartu in 1939–40. Wartime seasons between 1941 and 1944 were either unfinished or considered unofficial.

name: Meistriliiga
content:
The Meistriliiga, also known as the Premium Liiga for sponsorship reasons, is the top division of football in Estonia. Founded in 1992 after the country regained independence, it replaced the earlier national championship system that had been interrupted during the Soviet era. The league currently features 10 clubs, operates on a four-round format, and runs from March to November due to seasonal weather conditions.

Historically, the roots of Estonian football date back to 1921, when the first national championship was held. After decades of interruption under Soviet rule, the modern Meistriliiga marked a return to independent competition. Over time, the league evolved from semi-professional to fully professional status in 2020, supported by financial mechanisms from the national association. Broadcasting has also expanded, with matches now shown both domestically and internationally.

In terms of competition, the bottom club is relegated to the Esiliiga, while the second-to-last team faces a relegation play-off. FC Flora is the most successful club in league history, holding the record for the most titles, including the 2025 championship.

name: Estonian Cup
content:
The Estonian Cup is the main domestic knockout football tournament in Estonia. It was first held in 1938, with Sport Tallinn becoming the inaugural winner. After only two pre-war editions, the competition was interrupted due to World War II and the Soviet occupation, before being reintroduced in 1992 following Estonia’s regained independence.

The tournament follows a knockout format and includes clubs from different levels of the Estonian football pyramid, giving smaller teams a chance to compete against top-tier sides. The winner of the cup typically qualifies for European competitions, most recently earning a place in the UEFA Conference League qualifiers.

In the modern era, the most successful clubs include FCI Levadia and FC Flora, both of which have won the trophy multiple times. Other notable winners include Narva Trans and Nõmme Kalju. The competition remains an important part of Estonian football, often producing dramatic finals and opportunities for clubs outside the top division to achieve success.
